title: Multi-Collector ICP-MS Analyser

blocks.name: mc_reduction
fields: Internal Normalization Element and Isotope Ratio

notes: The multi-collector mass analyser: Faraday array and amplifiers, block/cycle acquisition structure, and the reduction steps that simultaneous collection makes possible (mass fractionation law, internal normalisation, double spike). Independent of how sample reaches the plasma, so it composes with either a solution introduction system or a laser front end.
extraction: Extracted 2026-08-08 under Rule 6.10. Content taken from Solution MC-ICP-MS v5, whose descriptions are consistently 2-3x more developed than the geochronology TAPP's and whose tiers are C=Basic where the geochronology TAPP has C=Advanced — Test 4 established that 81% of that TAPP's tier differences were drift. Unusually well evidenced: these same 13 fields were independently identified months earlier as the MC-only content of the LA-ICP-MS Geochronology TAPP.
decisions: 2026-08-08, from Phase 0 for LA-MC-ICP-MS against Zhang et al. 2022. (a) Baseline Measurement Approach offered only beam deflection or acid-blank aspiration; neither is possible during laser ablation, where background is collected as laser-off cycles at the start of the block. Description broadened to cover all three. (b) Added Peak Flatness Method and Threshold / Peak Flatness. The paper tunes for 'optimum peak flatness'; this is specific to simultaneous collection and was absent from the whole library. Split into criterion and measured value per the Oxide Production precedent, which names peak flatness as an instance.

Column I (Keyed By) added to every field 2026-08-11 under Rule 7; owned_columns gained "I". Module-owned, so the value is authoritative for all consumers. Also 2026-08-11: descriptions gained an explicit 'Record N/A where...' condition under Rule 7 A.4, propagated to all consumers by recomposition.

2026-08-12: version 3 -> 4 with NO content change. composed_tapps.json recorded MCICPMS v4 against all 3 consumers while this manifest said 3 — the same drift found in Module_ReportingCore the same day, and resolved the same way: the register is written per TAPP by the composition tooling, the manifest is hand-edited, so the manifest is the likelier one to have been missed. Setting it to 4 makes the two agree without asserting a content change that did not happen. Found by the audit behind check_module_versions().

2026-08-12: Collector Configuration `defines: channel` -> `defines: channel per analyte`, and its description now asks for the analyte each cup serves. Closes the binding gap in the three multicollector TAPPs: 7.4b makes Collector Configuration the channel definer where a cup array exists, which demotes Monitored Isotopes to plain `analyte` — and that demotion had silently dropped the channel-to-analyte binding, leaving it recoverable only by parsing element symbols out of the free-text cup string, which 7.3.1 forbids. Monitor cups carry no parent, which the nullable-parent semantics of 7.3.1 already cover.

2026-08-14: source_comment declared. Rule 6.11 originally withheld the label from the general modules as noise; with 12 modules supplying most of the library, naming the source of every field is what makes a composed TAPP readable. Documentation only — no structural meaning, not schema content.

2026-08-25: Step 1 of the Description/Purpose split. Column B keeps the Description sentences; the Purpose sentences moved to consumer-owned Column J. Move only — no text reworded or deleted. Routing and rules in analysis/Step1_Routing_ALL_MODULES_2026-08-25.csv.
